# exa-search-cli

> A command-line integration with Exa for repeatable research: web search, readable page-text retrieval, and external research tasks with structured output.

## Contribution and scope

Built with AI coding agents as part of Nolan Vale's independent product and workflow-automation work. Nolan defines requirements, directs implementation, checks results, and iterates. Exa provides the underlying search and research services; this repository supplies a CLI integration, not a new search engine or AI model.

## Install

```bash
uv tool install exa-search-cli
```

Alternatively, use pip install exa-search-cli in a suitable Python environment.

Set EXA_API_KEY to an authorized Exa API key. Do not commit or expose the key.

## Commands

- `exa-search <query>`: search. Flags: --json, --num-results, --type, --category, --start-date, --end-date, --include-domain, --exclude-domain, --similar, --text.
- `exa-crawl <url>`: request readable page text. Flags: --json, --max-chars.
- `exa-research <topic>`: create a research task on Exa. Flags: --json, --model.
- `exa-research-status <research-id>`: check a task and retrieve its result. Flags: --json.

Source access, categories, models, and result availability depend on the provider.

## Workflow examples

```bash
exa-search "document review workflow" --json
exa-crawl https://example.com -c 8000
exa-research "document processing approaches" --json
exa-research-status <research-id> --json
```

## Output reference

- Search: results[]{title, url, published_date, author, highlights[], text}.
- Crawl: results[]{url, title, text}.
- Research/status: {research_id, model, instructions, status, output.content, error}.
- Result iterator for object or array responses: (if type=="array" then . else (.results // []) end)[].

Consult README.md and docs/USAGE.md for examples and installed-command help for supported options.

## Data and review

Requests are sent to Exa. Research commands create external tasks, so the integration is not entirely read-only or offline. Protect credentials and review generated research against source material before using it in decisions.

## Key files

- README.md: purpose, contribution, setup, and limitations.
- AGENTS.md: agent integration guidance.
- docs/USAGE.md: usage reference.
- pyproject.toml: dependencies and entry points.
